text:
incident-bot: Pager: SRE @channel — Multiple customers reporting failed billing webhooks and seat syncs. Observed spike in webhook 429s and 402/403 responses from Stripe starting ~1855554200. Paging on-call.

Alex: on it. I'm triaging, grabbing logs and rate-limit counters. First-pass: are webhooks being retried? any queue backlog?

Mira: I see delivery_errors in infra metrics: webhook_delivery.errors.v2 increased from ~2/min to >120/min across multiple queues, with backend response codes 429 and 402. CPU on webhook workers OK. Delivery latency spiked.

Sam: billing FYI — if webhooks for invoice.payment_succeeded fail, customers might not get entitlement updates. We already have a handful of customers complaining about seat access.

Jas: Support got multiple tickets: "Seats suddenly locked", "Invoice not applied". Tickets link: https://support.internal/tickets?q=webhook%20stripe

Alex: quick checklist: 1) confirm Stripe status page, 2) check our webhook retry logic/queue length, 3) assess whether Stripe has applied quota or enforcement, 4) enable fallback poller for critical customers, 5) notify customers with outage advisory if needed.

Stripe Status Bot: Stripe incident: rate-limit/quota enforcement for partner API region (https://status.stripe.com/incidents/abcd). They acknowledge enforcement on certain accounts for unpaid invoice/billing restraint.

Mira: Correlation: our failed responses line up with Stripe `quota_exceeded` responses for our webhook partner token. We see both 429 and a body with: `{"error": {"type":"rate_limit","message":"Quota enforcement: partner has exceeded allowed request units"}}`.

Alex: Good catch. That explains external 429/402. Action plan: (A) switch critical customers to poller + backfill queue, (B) enable verbose retry in our webhook worker with exponential backoff and jitter, (C) open emergency request with Stripe, (D) throttle non-critical webhook consumers to reduce load.

Mira: Implementing (A) now: enabling polling fallback for customers with >$threshold monthly revenue and those flagged P0. Command I'm running:

```
# enable poller for critical customers
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $INTERNAL_TOKEN" \
  https://internal-api.redwood/v1/ops/poller/enable \
  -d '{"selector":"revenue>10000 OR tag:enterprise","interval":"5m"}'
```

DevOps Bot: job scheduled: poller-enable job queued (job id: poller-2026-18555545).

Alex: I'm increasing internal webhook queue retention and kicking the backfill worker. Backfill will attempt delivery with 30s initial backoff, max retries 12.

```
# adjust worker config
kubectl -n prod set env deploy/webhook-worker MAX_RETRIES=12 BASE_BACKOFF=30
```

Sam: Re: customer impact — preliminary estimate: ~8 enterprise customers impacted by delayed entitlement changes; ~120 SMB customers experiencing delayed invoices. Finance impact: potential delays in billing recognition, but no automated stops expected if backfills succeed within 24h.

Jas: Messaging draft for status page and support auto-responses: short, clear, avoid blaming Stripe. Proposed: "We are experiencing delayed billing updates and seat syncs due to an upstream rate-limiting incident affecting webhook delivery. Our teams are running fallback polling and backfills; services should be restored for most customers within a few hours. Contact support for urgent access needs." :megaphone:

Alex: +1. I'm sending on #status-updates now. Also creating a short internal runbook tick to escalate if backfills not progressing after 2 hours.

Mira: Stripe support ticket opened (ticket #ST-98765). They responded: "partner quota enforcement triggered by sudden burst from your webhook pool; provide mitigation plan and we can expedite temporary soft limit increase." I've attached delivery logs and our mitigation steps.

Alex: I'm preparing the mitigation plan: 1) reduce webhook fanout for events we can consolidate, 2) enable poller for critical customers, 3) stagger retry windows, 4) apply rate-limiter on our side to smooth bursts.

Mira: Quick config change done: webhook fanout reduced from 1->N to batched deliveries for invoice.* and payment_intent.* where multiple events were being sent. Patch: `gateway:batch_window=2s`.

DevOps Bot: deploy succeeded: webhook-gateway v3.14.2 -> v3.14.3 (batch window change).

Alex: Monitoring delivery success: backfill worker processed 3.2k events in the first 18 minutes; successful deliveries started to trickle in for priority customers. Retention queue reduced by ~40%.

Sam: Noting potential billing gap: one enterprise customer (CustID: C-4421) reported immediate seat loss for ~10 users. We're manually reconciling entitlements and will offer temporary override until backfill completes.

Jas: Doing manual customer outreach to affected accounts: templates ready, will include ETA and workaround (manual entitlement refresh from admin console).

Mira: Observability note: our alerting threshold for webhook_delivery.errors is too tight during partner-rate-limit events; suggest adding a suppression rule when upstream returns `quota_exceeded` to avoid alert fatigue. Filing a ticket: INFRA-4321.

Alex: Agreed. Also let's add a health-check to detect `quota_exceeded` payloads and surface them separately in the incidents dashboard.

Stripe Status Bot: Update: Stripe issued a temporary uplift for our partner token while they process the request — please limit burst traffic while uplift is in place.

Mira: We're throttling aggressive producers now (services: webhook-ingress, billing-sync-producer). Running `traffic-shaper` job to cap RPS to stripe-friendly windows.

Alex: Final short summary for postmortem: root cause — upstream quota enforcement by Stripe due to sudden webhook burst/fanout from our integration. Contributing factors — lack of local smoothing, high fanout for duplicate events, insufficient fallback priority for pollers. Mitigations applied — polling fallback enabled for critical customers, backfill retries increased, fanout batching, temporary throttle, Stripe uplift requested and applied, support & customer comms.

Sam: Will prepare customer remediation billing note for finance ops and customer success (credits if entitlements remained blocked >8h).

Jas: Support remains on rotation for next 4 hours; will escalate any P0 customer requests to Alex directly.

Alex: I'll keep this thread updated. If things look stable in the next 90 minutes I'll hand off to next on-call. :white_check_mark: 

Mira: Logging follow-ups: INFRA-4321 (alert suppression), PLAT-2107 (add quota-detection metric), DOCS-118 (runbook update).

DevOps Bot: handoff scheduled with next on-call at 1855557600.

Alex: handoff: Mira will take over monitoring; I'm tagging as mitigated but not resolved. Last check: webhook error rate down ~75% from peak.

Mira: Acknowledged, monitoring.

incident-bot: Incident state changed: mitigated -> watch.

Alex: End update.
